searches.query: new AI automation tools released this week
searches.answer: Proton has launched Lumo Desktop, a privacy-focused AI assistant, for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Unlike other desktop apps, Lumo lets users control exactly which actions the AI agent can perform automatically, which require approval, and which are blocked entirely. It connects to local files, Proton email, Dropbox, Confluence, and Jira, and supports MCP servers. Proton vows no ad targeting or AI training on user data, keeps no server-side logs, and stores data on Swiss servers. Additionally, Microsoft has launched MAI Licensed Weights, allowing organizations to deploy and customize Microsoft AI models within their own Azure environments.
